svg.aria-label: Inbound call quality report: 14 dental clinic calls graded by an LLM judge
svg.title: Dental clinic inbound call quality report
svg.text: Parramatta Dental Clinic AI receptionist · Vapi voice agent orchestrated by n8n · every call graded after the fact by the same LLM-as-judge
The outbound campaign's rubric, unchanged: clarity, tone, flow, and whether the caller was guided to a clear next step. Most calls land Neutral — a verdict
that reads as "nothing went wrong" rather than "something went well".
The agent's share of the words spoken, recomputed from the word counts. If talking too
much were the problem, the dots would march left as the grade improves. They do not.
How the call ended, not whether an appointment was booked.
Booking outcome appears only in the prose summary, so this
figure does not claim a booking rate.
Both timeouts fell on calls the judge graded Neutral; no Good call
Read from the prose: 3 summaries name a date for the appointment —
the same 3 calls the judge graded Good. One summary says the
booking could not be completed, and the judge graded that call
Vapi bills per minute, so cost tracks call length: duration accounts for 97% of the variance in spend here (r = 0.99). The spread around the line is still
real — only 4 of the 14 calls land within 5% of it — so the rate is a good planning number and a poor per-call prediction.
The two longest calls are the same length to within two seconds — 4m 41s at $0.38, 4m 39s at $0.47.
Data quality — what the log got wrong
Found by building this figure. Each item is a reason to read one exported row as a claim, not a fact.
bot_word_percent is unusable on 5 of 16 graded rows — the most recent read 11,706,000% to 11,910,000%, which matches neither the word counts nor the call
duration. Talk share in this figure is recomputed from bot_word_count and user_word_count, which are consistent on every row.
One call was written to the log twice, byte-identical in every field — a retried write that a unique key on the call id would have prevented.
A second call was written twice with the same transcript but a different summary and a different judge justification — the grader is a sampling model, so the
same transcript does not reliably produce the same verdict. Any per-call grade is one draw, not the answer.
One row is entirely empty — which is why 17 records hold 16 graded rows and 14 distinct calls.
The phone column carries three different mask formats — it cannot be used as a join or upsert key until that is normalised.
Source: dentalClinic/DentalCallLogs.csv — 14 distinct graded calls made to one clinic over twelve days. Still a small sample: it demonstrates the grading pipeline on real
conversations and shows which signals do not hold up, not a quality rate for the agent.
Generated by charts/generate_charts.py from the judge's CSV output.
